cards.title: A distribution easy for read-once branching programs but hard for AC⁰ samplers
cards.formal: Does there exist a family of distributions D_n on {0,1}^n that can be generated by small-width read-once branching programs in the source’s layered-output model, but cannot be generated by polynomial-size constant-depth Boolean circuits? The requested direction is ROBP-easy and AC⁰-hard. The source leaves the precise ROBP resource bounds and the sampling-error requirement unspecified, so this is not yet a fully quantified separation claim.
cards.why: Would distinguish the power of shallow parallel generation from sequential generation with limited memory, complementing the separation already known in the other direction.
cards.status_note: Read the exact ROBP output conventions, the opposite-direction theorem and both future-directions paragraphs. Searches through 12 September 2026 found no result resolving the intended reverse separation. Quantitative resources and sampling error still require specification.

progress.text: The paper separates AC⁰-easy distributions from ROBP sampling and leaves the reverse direction open in both checked versions.

cards.definitions: For a finite set Ω, a probability distribution assigns nonnegative masses summing to one. A sampler is a deterministic function of independent uniformly random input bits; its output distribution is the pushforward of the uniform distribution. The source’s multi-output ROBP has ℓ+1 layers, each with at most w states, one start state, and exactly two outgoing edges at each nonfinal state, labeled 0 and 1. At step i it reads the i-th fresh random bit and follows that edge. Each edge carries a finite output string; all edges between the same pair of layers have the same output length γᵢ, with Σᵢγᵢ=n. Output is the concatenation along the path, and cannot subsequently be reread or changed. The width w is memory capacity in states, corresponding to at most ⌈log₂w⌉ bits for the state. An AC⁰ sampler family consists of Boolean circuits with n designated outputs, AND/OR gates of unbounded fan-in and NOT gates, with a depth bound d independent of n and size at most C(n+1)^a for constants C,a. Each circuit receives independent fair random bits; random-input nodes are counted in its size so their number is polynomially bounded. Exact sampling means equality of distributions. Total-variation distance between D,E on {0,1}^n is (1/2)Σ_z|D(z)−E(z)|; approximate sampling requires this to be at most a specified tolerance. The source does not select a tolerance or quantitative w(n),ℓ(n), and does not require a uniform circuit/program construction.
cards.answer_criterion: Specify the intended ROBP width/length and exact or approximate sampling convention, then prove or refute existence of a distribution family separated in this direction against every AC⁰ family. For a positive answer, the lower bound must exclude all such circuit samplers at the stated error, not merely circuits computing one chosen encoding of the sampler. The already known AC⁰-easy/ROBP-hard direction does not answer this question.

cards.title: Does small proof space imply short tree-like resolution refutations?
cards.formal: For μ equal to resolution clause space CSpace or PCR monomial space MSpace_K, does there exist a constant a≥1 and C>0 such that every unsatisfiable CNF F on n≥2 variables satisfies log₂(S_T(F)+1)≤C((μ(F)+1)log₂(n+1))^a? Determine the validity of this comparison in each of the two cases in the source’s Problem 5.1. For monomial space, K is an arbitrary fixed field and the constants may depend on K, but not on F or n. Here S_T is minimum tree-like resolution leaf count. The opposite comparison, bounding each space measure by logarithmic tree-like size up to these polynomial/logarithmic losses, is known.
cards.why: Would determine whether low working memory in propositional refutations fundamentally limits repeated work, clarifying strong size-space trade-offs and the cost of converting reusable proofs into trees.

cards.definitions: A literal is xᵢ or its negation ¬xᵢ. A clause is a disjunction of literals and a CNF F is a finite conjunction of clauses over variables x₁,…,xₙ; unsatisfiable means no Boolean assignment satisfies every clause. Resolution derives C∨D from C∨xᵢ and D∨¬xᵢ, and allows weakening from C to C∨D; input clauses can be used as axioms. A refutation derives the empty clause. A tree-like proof uses each derived occurrence as a premise at most once, duplicating occurrences when necessary; S_T(F) is the minimum number of leaves, rather than total literal count. A configuration proof starts with no stored clauses and at each step downloads an input clause, erases a stored clause, or adds a resolvent/weakening of clauses currently stored; it ends with the empty clause stored. CSpace(F) is the minimum, over such proofs with unrestricted length, of the maximum number of simultaneously stored clauses. For PCR fix K and use the polynomial ring K[x₁,…,xₙ,y₁,…,yₙ], where yᵢ represents ¬xᵢ. A line P means P=0. Logical axioms are z²−z for each z among xᵢ,yᵢ and xᵢ+yᵢ−1. The encoding of a clause is the product of its false-literal indicators: xᵢ contributes yᵢ and ¬xᵢ contributes xᵢ. From P,Q derive αP+βQ for α,β∈K; from P derive zP for any literal variable z. A PCR refutation derives 1. Its configurations may download axioms, erase lines or add an inference whose premises are stored. The monomial space of a configuration is the number of distinct formal monomials with nonzero coefficients occurring anywhere in its stored polynomials, counted once across all lines; coefficients and exponents are not separately charged. MSpace_K(F) is the minimum maximum monomial space over all PCR refutations. Every proof is finite and minima concern the specified syntactic systems. The source’s relation A⪯B permits A(F)≤((B(F))log n)^{O(1)}; ≈ means both directions. The harmless +1 terms here cover one-leaf or other constant-size cases. No polynomial-length restriction is imposed on the space-minimizing proof.
cards.answer_criterion: For each stated space measure, prove the universal polynomial/logarithmic simulation bound or refute it by showing that no constants C,a work for all unsatisfiable formulas (with K fixed in the PCR case). The two variants must be reported separately. A polynomial separation between raw measures does not refute a comparison that explicitly permits arbitrary polynomial and logarithmic factors.

cards.title: Efficient equations for VP with unrestricted complex coefficients
cards.formal: For every fixed integer c≥1, do there exist nonzero polynomials P_n in N_n=binom(n+n^c,n) coefficient variables, with degree and algebraic circuit size at most C_c N_n^{a_c}, such that for every fixed integer b≥1 there is n₀(c,b) for which P_n(coeff(f))=0 whenever n≥n₀(c,b) and f∈ℂ[x₁,…,xₙ] has total degree at most n^c and an algebraic circuit of size at most n^b? Constants C_c,a_c and the family (P_n) may depend on c, but not on b. Coefficients of f may be arbitrary complex numbers. This expresses the source’s eventual vanishing on every polynomial-size family, without demanding a common finite threshold across all circuit-size exponents.
cards.why: Would clarify whether a broad family of algebraic lower-bound certificates can recognize all efficiently computable polynomials once arbitrary coefficients are allowed.

cards.definitions: An algebraic circuit over ℂ is a finite directed acyclic graph with inputs x₁,…,xₙ and arbitrary complex constants, binary addition and multiplication gates, and one output. Subtraction is allowed via multiplication by −1; there are no division gates. Its size is its number of vertices. It computes an exact formal polynomial, and each constant is one field element regardless of its bit description. VP_ℂ consists of polynomial families with polynomially bounded total degree and polynomially bounded nonuniform algebraic circuit size. For d=n^c, list all monomials x₁^{α₁}⋯xₙ^{αₙ} with αᵢ≥0 and Σᵢαᵢ≤d in a fixed lexicographic order of exponent vectors. There are N_n=binom(n+d,n) such monomials. coeff(f) is the full vector of their coefficients, including zeros. P_n is a polynomial over ℂ whose variables are these N_n coordinates. Nonzero means not the zero formal polynomial; over ℂ it is equivalent to being nonzero at some coefficient vector. Both degree and circuit size of P_n are bounded by a fixed polynomial in N_n, not in n. The equations themselves are nonuniform: there is no additional requirement to construct their circuits in polynomial time from n. Vanishing must hold for all circuits under each fixed polynomial size bound eventually; the threshold can depend on that bound. Restricting c,b to positive integers covers arbitrary fixed polynomial exponents by increasing them. The statement imposes no bound on output coefficients of f or on constants used inside its circuit, and requests no explicit hard polynomial on which P_n is nonzero.
cards.answer_criterion: Prove existence of such a nontrivial polynomial-degree, polynomial-circuit-size family for every c, or refute the universal existence statement for at least one c. Vanishing only on polynomials with bounded integer coefficients, or only on a fixed restricted circuit architecture, does not establish the claim. Nonexistence of equations for VNP alone does not refute existence for VP.

context_blocks.title: An equation is a test on the whole coefficient vector
context_blocks.text: The input to P_n is the description of another polynomial by all its coefficients. An equation vanishes on easy polynomials and is nonzero somewhere else. Its efficiency is measured against this much larger coefficient-vector dimension.

context_blocks.title: The bounded-coefficient theorem concerns output polynomials
context_blocks.text: The known positive result restricts the final polynomial’s coefficients, for example to {−1,0,1}. Its computing circuit may still use arbitrary complex constants internally. Removing that semantic restriction is the question here.

context_blocks.title: The relevant existence notion is nonuniform
context_blocks.text: The source’s phrase “efficiently constructible equations” is formalized by membership in VP. The checked revision explicitly describes its upper-bound proofs as existential; the card therefore does not add a uniform circuit-generation algorithm.

context_blocks.title: The conditional VNP theorem leaves VP undecided
context_blocks.text: Under sufficiently strong permanent hardness, the source rules out efficient equations for VNP over characteristic-zero fields. Since VP is a smaller class, an equation vanishing on VP need not vanish on VNP, so the theorem does not answer this card.

methodology: Detailed cards have individually written statements, context, significance, and documented results. Source notes are unfinished research records and do not yet meet that standard. The legacy index is retained for traceability.
Open in the source means open at the date of that source. The build date, 10 September 2026, does not establish current open status. Old excerpts may omit conditions or subsequent results.

Selection considers model power, necessary resources, sharp bounds, structural characterizations, explicit constructions, and minimal assumptions. Source notes use a heuristic screen; detailed cards give an individual explanation.

The earlier automatic paper screen allowed at most one new card per paper title and rejected identical formulations and close duplicates within a source. Approved textbook and survey imports retain multiple distinct questions per publication. Confirmed overlaps supplement existing cards; collection-wide semantic deduplication remains incomplete.

Short quotations retain the source language. Later related literature, where listed, is a research aid rather than evidence of resolution. Personal notes and saved cards are stored locally in your browser.

Textbook and survey questions are dated paraphrases; source locations, conjectures, research directions and caveats are preserved on the problem cards. These annotations do not establish current open status or change a later card review. New source drafts remain unassessed for importance. The reader contains the imported questions and external bibliographic references only; source files are not bundled.

Selection groups follow the agreed 10 large and 25 small categories. We aim for benchmarks of 100 and 500 problems, with a possible expansion to 1,000. All three use the same category order and the same ranking within each category. The respective prefixes are 5/2, 25/10 and 50/20 problems per large/small category. The possible 1,000-problem expansion has 1000 assigned places and 0 reserved places. Each card records its category explicitly. These counts describe saved candidates; classification does not verify a statement or its current open status. Deleted records are absent from the catalogue and exports. Their stable IDs and reasons are retained to prevent reimport. Final quota selection and a comprehensive deduplication audit remain pending.

The category-wide review also uses shared priority bands for questions of comparable scope; it does not claim that these ties have a scientifically meaningful internal order. Unassessed drafts share a provisional score of 50; their relative order is only an ID tie-break, not an importance judgment. The first 5/2 places in each large/small category are an explicit editorial focus selection balancing importance and topical diversity. Focus ordering does not alter importance scores; remaining candidates use score and ID order. The targets are 100 and 500 problems, with a possible expansion to 1,000. Top 100, Top 500 and the possible Top 1000 use the first 5/2, 25/10 and 50/20 category places respectively, all from the same ranking.
